Welcome to the new Kairos Lab blog. This is the first test post, here to check that Hugo + Stack renders everything properly: headings, table of contents, code blocks, the cover image, word count, and estimated reading time.
If you can see this post, the blog is live.
Why Hugo + Stack Hugo is a static site generator written in Go, and its biggest strength is speed: even a thousand posts build in seconds. It needs no database and no server — push the Markdown and it becomes a website.
Stack is a card-style Hugo theme made for blogging, and it ships with:
Responsive layout that looks good on phones and computers A dark-mode toggle in the top right Local search, archives, categories, and tags Table of contents, reading time, and related-post recommendations Previewing locally and publishing When writing locally, start the preview server first — save a change and it shows up in the browser right away:
1 2 3 4 # Start the local preview (-D shows drafts too) hugo server -D # Open http://localhost:1313 Once it looks right, push to GitHub and Actions builds and publishes it automatically:
1 2 3 git add content/post/kairos-blog-test.md git commit -m "Publish test post" git push origin main What a post’s front matter looks like Every post starts with front matter — the title, date, categories, and tags:
1 2 3 4 5 6 7 --- title: "I Saved 1,000 Articles — Why Can't I Use a Single One?" date: 2026-11-14 categories: ["From Collecting to a Second Brain"] tags: ["Knowledge Management", "Collecting", "Inbox"] draft: false --- A post with draft: true is a draft and won’t be published; set it to false and it appears on the site.
What’s coming next The first real post is already written: “I Saved 1,000 Articles — Why Can’t I Use a Single One?”, built on my own numbers: 621 notes, 337 sitting in the Inbox, and only 16 in the knowledge base.
Once this test post confirms the layout is fine, Episode 1 goes out. Stay tuned.
title: Test Post: Kairos Lab Blog Is Live
